GA-2025-HB1020.s: The law changes the Georgia Judicial Retirement System so people can get monthly retirement benefits for service as a district attorney starting at age 65. It also changes how benefits are figured for people who join after the law takes effect and how survivor benefits are calculated. It became law as Act 716 and takes effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB1090.s: The law changes how Echols County commissioners are chosen. It moves all county commissioner races to countywide elections, instead of using commission districts, and lets current members stay in office until their terms end. It takes effect on January 1, 2027.

GA-2025-HB1097.s: Georgia now requires certain mental health facilities to check the criminal record, license status, and registry status of owners, applicants, and employees. The state Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Disabilities may send fingerprints to state and federal law enforcement systems for these checks and keep personnel files. It also sets steps for dealing with people found ineligible. It became law in 2026 and took effect July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB115.s: Passed law changes Georgia rules for vessel registration with the Department of Natural Resources. It would require certain notice when a vessel is registered, allow checks on unattended vessels, and let the department seek repayment for the cost of removing, storing, and disposing of abandoned vessels. It became Act 434 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB1185.s: The law moves certain shareholder claims to Georgia’s state business court. It also lets a company’s bylaws or charter require some claims to be heard there, and it covers when claims can be moved to that court and when attorney fees and costs may be paid. It became law as Act 460 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB1254.s: The law moves regulation of several professions from individual boards to the Secretary of State in Georgia. It also changes parts of the state code for cemetery and funeral services, DNA testing, and other professions and businesses rules. It became law as Act 473 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB1268.s: Georgia updated and cleaned up parts of its state law code. The measure revised and reenacted parts of the code, removed old or conflicting text, and added some court-made rules from state Supreme Court decisions. It became Act 723 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB1302.s: Creates a new Office of Education and Workforce Strategy in place of the Office of Student Achievement. It would also combine two state plans for jobs and career training, and set rules for registered apprenticeship programs. The Technical College System of Georgia would serve as the state apprenticeship agency. It became law as Act 474 and takes effect July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB134.s: The law changes Georgia sales tax rules for manufactured homes by revising and expanding the tax break for them. It also sets a sunset date and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB1344.s: Georgia’s insurance and traffic laws would be changed to give the Insurance Commissioner more power to enforce the rules. It would also clarify rules on insurance fraud, uninsured drivers, excluded drivers, premium tax, insurance rates, claims handling, and uninsured or unregistered motor vehicles. The bill became law as Act 635 and takes effect on January 1, 2027.

GA-2025-HB1514.s: Changes the date for electing the president of the Fulton County Board of Education. It affects the county school board and related election timing. The bill became law as Act 667 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB1536.s: Creates a new city charter for Eatonton, Georgia, and handles related changes. It also repeals specific old acts and any conflicting laws. The law became Act 583 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB1571.s: The law changes the court schedule for the State Court of Bryan County. It affects that county's state court and sets an effective date of July 1, 2026. It became Act 603.

GA-2025-HB1575.s: The law expands a City of Kingsland home tax break, called a homestead exemption, to residents age 62 or older. It applies to the city’s property taxes for city purposes. It became Act 683 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB651.s: The law changes rules for automated traffic enforcement devices in school zones, which are cameras or other tools that record speeding. It also lets district attorneys and similar local prosecutors enforce civil fines tied to school zone speeding cases based on recorded images. It became law as Act 711 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB739.s: The bill would add certain land to the City of Lawrenceville through annexation, which means bringing new territory into the city limits. It would also provide for a public vote on the change. The act became law as Act 321 and takes effect on December 31, 2026.

GA-2025-HB90.s: Georgia would raise the maximum acreage a property can have and still get a special tax break for bona fide conservation use land, which is land kept in conservation use. It affects property owners who want that lower tax treatment. The law was signed and takes effect on January 1, 2027.

GA-2025-HB945.s: Georgia's banking and finance rules would be updated to let banks place a hold on an eligible adult's account if they suspect financial exploitation, and to set rules for adding and removing that hold. It would also change some credit report rules and add steps for cease and desist orders, court review, and required disclosures for people involved in litigation finance. The bill became law as Act 478 and took effect July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HB952.s: The bill changes the Bulloch County board of elections and registration by increasing it to five members. It also updates how those members are appointed and sets temporary terms for the new seats. It became law as Act 646 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HR1008.s: This resolution ratifies changes to Georgia’s statewide water management plan. It affects how the state plan is put into effect and how it is read. It became law as Act 425 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-HR251.s: Georgia law now changes the state constitution so probate judges must be elected in nonpartisan elections, meaning without party labels on the ballot. It affects probate judges and local elections. The measure became Act 638 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB111.s: Georgia’s consumer privacy law would set rules for how businesses handle people’s personal data. It covers things like notices, data security, who must follow the rules, and some exceptions. It became law as Act 462 and takes effect July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB143.s: The law changes the Georgia Firefighter's Pension Fund so certain members can retire at age 50. It also lets the fund invest in some assets rated below investment grade, which means lower-rated and riskier investments. It became Act 630 and took effect July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB146.s: The law updates state rules for cemeteries and burial grounds. It also changes how permits are handled for moving human remains from one burial place to another and adds definitions for some terms. It became Act 486 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB148.s: The law creates a pilot program for outdoor learning spaces in public schools. It also calls for an evaluation of the pilot and a report on the results. It became law as Act 398 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB150.s: The law extends a program that lets public school systems hire some Teachers Retirement System of Georgia beneficiaries as full-time classroom teachers through June 30, 2034. It also lowers the work history needed to qualify from 30 years to 25 years. The law took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB160.s: This law changes the penalty for a second reckless stunt driving offense by letting a court order a device that limits a vehicle’s speed instead of taking the vehicle away. It also sets rules for when that order can be used, tells the Department of Revenue, and takes effect July 1, 2028.

GA-2025-SB162.s: Georgia law now requires the Georgia Composite Medical Board to set up an automated system for checking the credentials of healthcare providers in the state. The board must also meet any related requirements tied to that system. The measure became Act 408 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB216.s: The law lets people hired as the director of the Prosecuting Attorneys Qualifications Commission join the Georgia Judicial Retirement System. It also covers an option for current workers, moving funds, paying the system’s cost, and counting some past service and pay for retirement benefits. The law took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB285.s: Georgia law changes how some 9-1-1 charge money is sent to the Peace Officers' Annuity and Benefit Fund. It also raises monthly benefits under the state's retirement benefit rules. The law became Act 416 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB293.s: Georgia would increase the number of free license plates given to certain veterans. It affects veterans who qualify for these plates under state law. The law became Act 503 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB369.s: Creates a new kind of charter school called a completion charter school in Georgia. It also sets rules and standards for these schools and lets existing charter schools convert to them. The law took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB383.s: Georgia passed this law to change how local child fatality review committees review child deaths. It adds members to the committees, requires training attendance, and changes how coroner or medical examiner offices and the committees identify which child deaths must be reviewed. It also changes report deadlines and other review rules. It became law on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB384.s: Georgia law now lets some vehicle owners choose a five-year registration and revalidation period instead of a shorter one. It also updates related legal terms and makes matching changes in the state motor vehicle laws. The law takes effect on July 1, 2027.

GA-2025-SB395.s: The bill became law and requires a doctor to send certain information to the Georgia Composite Medical Board when certifying someone for the Low THC Oil Patient Registry. It also calls for yearly reports and lets the Department of Public Health share certain information. The law took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB406.s: The act would require property owners' associations to register with the state and keep that registration up to date. It would also set up a state board to review complaints and allow appeals. The law also changes when associations can place liens and use assessments against lot owners. It became law as Act 715 and takes effect January 1, 2027.

GA-2025-SB420.s: Georgia would add fees for reef fish and migratory fish endorsements, which are added permits for certain fishing. It would also change the effective dates for some related rules and penalties. The law became Act 508 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB428.s: The law directs Georgia’s Department of Community Health to ask the federal government for approval to let some home and community-based services qualify for Medicaid payment. It would take effect only after that approval. It became Act 492 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB430.s: The law changes Georgia’s room tax rules so certain military museums can count as destination marketing groups and private nonprofit groups. That can affect how these museums are treated under the tax law for rooms, lodgings, and other places to stay. It became law as Act 493 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB435.s: The law renames the Georgia Development Authority as the Georgia Agricultural Development Authority. It also makes other small wording changes in state law to match the new name. It became law as Act 432 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB439.s: The law sets rules for referral agencies that help people find assisted living communities and personal care homes. It requires these agencies to give certain disclosures to future residents, get proof that the resident got them, charge and collect fees in set ways, and check that the homes are licensed. It became law as Act 510 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB444.s: The law says some insurance coverage decisions for health care services in Georgia cannot be based only on artificial intelligence or other software tools. It changes rules for private review agents, which are the people or groups that review coverage requests for insurers. The law took effect on January 1, 2027.

GA-2025-SB447.s: The law changes how local officials handle some permits tied to soil erosion and sediment control. It tells local issuing authorities to give rejected applicants a written list of reasons for denial within set time limits, and it adds general rules for counties and cities on accepting, denying, or not accepting certain permits. It became Act 513 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB452.s: Georgia Act 414 would raise the highest amount the state can put into a 401(k) for certain state law enforcement officers. It also sets out some definitions and a start date. The bill became law and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB470.s: Georgia made a law that bans people from possessing, using, making, selling, offering, distributing, or bringing in signal jammers, which are devices that block signals. It also lets the Attorney General start court action to take these devices away and allows some exemptions. The law became Act 495 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB485.s: Georgia law now lets people who are in the final semester of a master’s social work program take the social work licensing exam before they finish school. It affects applicants for a social work license in the state.

GA-2025-SB524.s: The law creates special Georgia license plates, including one honoring Girl Scouts of Georgia and one marking the 250th anniversary of the United States. It changes state rules for these plates and related payments. It became law in 2026 and takes effect on January 1, 2027.

GA-2025-SB540.s: Georgia law requires operators of conversational AI services to make certain disclosures and to give users some privacy tools. It also requires steps to limit some actions involving minors and a plan for how the system should respond to suicidal thoughts or self-harm. The attorney general can enforce it. It became law as Act 518 and takes effect on July 1, 2027.

GA-2025-SB551.s: This law would repeal Georgia rules tied to eggs in the state food rules. It affects food labeling and food safety rules for eggs. It became law as Act 433 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB556.s: Georgia’s law changes how grade point averages are figured for HOPE Scholarship and some other scholarships. It includes advanced placement and international baccalaureate fine arts courses in that calculation. The change took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB570.s: Georgia law now requires inns and short-term rental properties to have a human trafficking training program for staff. It also sets rules for training policies, record keeping, limits, and penalties. The law became Act 519 and takes effect July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB587.s: Georgia law creates an animal cruelty database. The Prosecuting Attorneys' Council of Georgia would create, run, and keep it, with rules for what it must include and how reports and forms are handled. It became law as Act 498 and takes effect July 1, 2026.

GA-2025-SB76.s: The law creates a specialty license plate that helps the Georgia Veterans Service Foundation. It became Act 485 and takes effect on July 1, 2027.

GA-2025-SR624.s: The resolution honors Officer Drew Haynes Brown and dedicates an intersection in Cobb County in his memory. It is a formal statement by lawmakers, not a law that sets new rules. It became Act 500 and took effect on July 1, 2026.

GA-2026SS-HB68.s: The bill would create a homestead tax break for homes in the City of Lyons, based on money from a new local sales tax in the area that includes Toombs County. It would set rules for who gets the break and how it works, and it would include a local vote and other required steps. The House first lost the bill, then reconsidered it and lost reconsideration on June 23, 2026.

GA-2026SS-HB70.s: The bill would create a homestead tax break for property owners in Toombs County. The amount would match the assessed value of the home, and it would be funded by a new local sales tax in the county's special district. It would also set rules for the exemption, call for a public vote, and include dates and repeal terms.

GA-2026SS-HB72.s: This bill would create a homestead tax break for homes in the City of Patterson. The break would be tied to a new local sales tax in the special district that matches Pierce County. It would affect homeowners in that area and set rules for how the break would work.

GA-2026SS-HB73.s: The bill would create a homestead tax break for homes in the City of East Dublin. It would be paid for by a new local sales tax in the special district that matches Laurens County, and it would apply to homeowners in that area.

GA-2026SS-HB75.s: The bill would create a homestead exemption from Lanier County property taxes for a home’s assessed value, based on a new local sales tax. The tax would apply in a special district that matches Lanier County. It would also set rules for the exemption, how it works, and a voter referendum.

GA-2026SS-HB78.s: The bill would create a homestead exemption from City of Tifton property taxes for homes in a special district tied to Tift County. The tax break would be based on a new Local Homestead Option Sales Tax in that district. It would also set rules for how the exemption would work and include a voter referendum.

GA-2026SS-HB79.s: The bill would create a homestead tax exemption in Tift County for the assessed value of a home, based on a new local sales tax in the same area. It would set the rules for the exemption, when it applies, and how it would be handled. It would also provide for a vote by local voters.

GA-2026SS-HB84.s: The bill would create a homestead exemption for City of Morgan property taxes on owner-occupied homes. The tax break would be tied to a new local sales tax in the special district that includes Calhoun County. It would affect homeowners in that area.

GA-2026SS-HB87.s: The bill would create a homestead exemption from City of West Point property taxes for homes in a special tax district in Harris County. The amount of the exemption would be tied to the yearly value set for the home and funded by a new local sales tax in that district. It also sets rules for how the exemption would work and includes a referendum, or voter vote, before it takes effect.

GA-2026SS-HB88.s: The bill would create a homestead tax exemption for homes in the City of Hogansville, based on the assessed value of the home. The exemption would be funded by a new local sales tax in a special district that matches Troup County. It would also set rules for how the exemption works and include a public vote.

GA-2026SS-HB89.s: The bill would create a homestead tax exemption for homes in the City of West Point, meaning part of the city property tax on a home could be removed. The exemption would be tied to a new local sales tax in the special district that matches Troup County, and voters would decide it in a referendum.

GA-2026SS-HR52.s: The resolution honors the lives and memory of Ava Olivia Derbecker and Faris Vincent Derbecker. It was adopted by the House.

GA-2026SS-HR54.s: A House resolution honors the anniversary of the U.S. Supreme Court’s Olmstead decision and the courage of the people who brought the case. It is a formal statement by lawmakers.

GA-2026SS-HR56.s: The resolution would recognize and honor the Democratic Republic of the Congo National Football Team for qualifying for and competing in the 2026 FIFA World Cup. It affects the team and is a formal statement by the Georgia House.

GA-2026SS-HR57.s: The resolution would recognize and honor the South Africa National Football Team for qualifying for and competing in the 2026 FIFA World Cup. It is a formal statement of support from the Georgia House.

GA-2026SS-SB10.s: The bill would require any existing special district sales tax (FLOST) to stop right before a local homestead option sales tax (LHOST) starts in the same county district. It would also change when the LHOST begins. It includes an effective date and would repeal conflicting laws.

GA-2026SS-SB3.s: The act creates a committee to set the specs, standards, and other rules for a new statewide election equipment system. It also spells out what the Secretary of State can do in picking, certifying, or buying that equipment, and it makes some actions void if they go beyond that authority. The law also changes the effective date of a 2024 elections law.

GA-2026SS-SB6.s: The bill would create a homestead tax break for homes in Stephens County. The break would match the assessed value of the home, based on money from a new local sales tax in a special district that covers the county. It would also set rules for how the exemption works and when it applies.

GA-2026SS-SR10.s: A state resolution that recognizes and commends Philadelphia Baptist Church on its 153rd anniversary. It is a formal statement from the Senate honoring the church.

GA-2026SS-SR13.s: The Georgia Senate adopted a resolution to recognize and commend Tayvian D. Allen. It is a formal statement of recognition for him.

GA-2026SS-SR14.s: The Senate adopted a resolution honoring the life and memory of Reverend Robert Lee Abrams and offering condolences. It is a formal statement by lawmakers about his life and service.
